ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the oneness of God?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia theological discourse, reinforces the concept of Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah by asserting that the true object of worship is exclusively One, rejecting all forms of polytheism (Shirk). It serves as a foundational creedal statement that underpins the Shia understanding of divine unity, distinguishing the singular, unique God from created beings and false deities. The declaration emphasizes not just God's existence, but His exclusive right to be worshipped, a core tenet in both Quranic exegesis and Shia jurisprudence.
